assignments.subject: Mathematics
assignments.title: Fractions on a number line
assignments.description: Practise placing and comparing fractions on a number line. Use the worksheet or work in your maths notebook.
instructions: Draw a number line from 0 to 1. Divide it into four equal intervals and mark each quarter.
Label 1/4 and 3/4. Write one sentence to explain how the number line shows which fraction is greater.
Draw a second number line divided into halves. Compare the two drawings and explain why 2/4 and 1/2 mark the same point. Bring your work to the next maths lesson.
assignments.askChild: Is 2/4 bigger, smaller or the same as 1/2? How can a number line prove it?

clarifications.title: Worksheet clarification
clarifications.text: You can complete the homework in your notebook. Printing is not required.

assignments.subject: English
assignments.title: Read chapter 4 and write a short summary
assignments.description: Read chapter 4 of your class reader and retell the main events in your own words.
instructions: Read at your own pace. Pause after each scene and say what happened in one sentence.
Write four or five sentences in your English notebook. Include the main character, the problem, and what changed.
assignments.askChild: What problem did the main character face in chapter 4, and what would you have done?

assignments.subject: Science
assignments.title: Observe how a seed germinates
assignments.description: Set up a simple observation using two beans and a damp paper towel.
instructions: Place the beans on a damp paper towel and keep them near a window.
Check the beans once a day. Record any changes to the seed coat and root. Use the observation notes or make your own table.
assignments.askChild: What does a seed need to start growing? Which one do you think matters most?

assignments.subject: Social Studies
assignments.title: Sketch a map of your neighbourhood
assignments.description: Make a simple map showing landmarks near your home.
instructions: Add three landmarks and a key. Use arrows to show the route from your home to one landmark.
assignments.askChild: If a friend visited, which route would you draw from our home to your school?

assignments.subject: English
assignments.title: Sort words by their prefixes
assignments.description: Group the words from class by their prefixes. Explain how each prefix changes the meaning.
instructions: Make columns for re-, un-, and pre-. Add at least three words to each column.

assignments.subject: Mathematics
assignments.title: Continue and explain number patterns
assignments.description: Find the rule for each number sequence from class.
instructions: Write the next three numbers. Describe each rule in a sentence.

assignments.subject: EVS
assignments.title: Write about one way your family can reuse materials at home
assignments.description: Choose an everyday item and describe a practical way to use it again.
instructions: Explain what the item was originally used for, how you repurposed it, and who could use it next.
assignments.askChild: Which thing at home do we throw away that we could reuse instead?

assignments.subject: Mathematics
assignments.title: Find 2D shapes at home
assignments.description: Look for circles, rectangles, and triangles around your home.
instructions: Draw one example of each shape and label where you found it.
assignments.askChild: How many shapes can you spot at the dinner table? Which one has the most corners?

assignments.subject: English
assignments.title: Read and reflect on a poem
assignments.description: Read the poem from class aloud and explain which image stood out to you.
instructions: Copy one line into your notebook and explain what it made you picture.
assignments.askChild: Which line of the poem would you read aloud to me, and why?
